acceptance: In a superseded run, the aggregate jobs conclude cancelled, not failure, in the PR check list.
A real upstream failure still makes the aggregate fail.
A run that was not superseded, but had an upstream job cancelled for another reason such as a timeout, still fails, and does not pass as cancelled.
context: See `scripts/ci_unit_result.py` (SUPERSEDED_EXIT_CODE), and the aggregate steps plus "Cancel superseded run so the aggregate concludes cancelled" in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (around lines 2170-2230).
description: When an upstream job is cancelled, `scripts/ci_unit_result.py` exits 3. The workflow then cancels its own run, so the run concludes "cancelled". The aggregate jobs themselves still conclude "failure", because they exited non-zero. On #2983 (run 38621020255) and #2995, the PR check list showed `core`, `docs`, `tooling`, `explorer`, `landing` and `results-data` as FAILURE, although each log says "CANCELLED (not failed)". Anyone reading PR status, people or agents, has to open every log to tell a real failure from a superseded run.
